name: Dipeptide-2

lead: Dipeptide-2 is a two-amino-acid peptide added to under-eye products to make puffy eyes look flatter and more rested.
It is part of the Eyeliss complex alongside hesperidin methyl chalcone and palmitoyl tetrapeptide-7.

paras: The manufacturer says it increases lymphatic circulation so fluid drains away from the eye area.
Used topically in cosmetics; the available evidence is a small manufacturer study of the full complex, and no independent trials were found.

chain: Dipeptide signals to boost lymphatic circulation
Less fluid retained under the eye
angle.text: Eye creams containing dipeptide-2 are used to make the under-eye area look less swollen. The mechanism, as described by the manufacturer, is improved drainage of fluid that makes bags look pronounced.

lead: Dipeptide-2 is a cosmetic peptide made of two amino acids, valine and tryptophan. It is used in eye serums, creams and gels to make the under-eye area look less puffy, so the eyes look flatter and more rested. Its manufacturer says it increases lymphatic circulation, helping fluid drain from the delicate eye area.[1]

It is one of three actives in Eyeliss, an ingredient complex that also contains hesperidin methyl chalcone and palmitoyl tetrapeptide-7, marketed as a combined approach to puffy eyes.[1] The manufacturer reports a 20-person study with a 3% concentration of the complex in which 70% of participants improved after 56 days.[1]

Puffiness around the eyes is described as arising mostly from fluid build-up, with ageing, allergy, sleep loss, salt intake and other factors involved.[2] Dipeptide-2 products aim at that fluid component, in the form of a topical product applied to the eye area.
infobox: Eyeliss complex (with hesperidin methyl chalcone and palmitoyl tetrapeptide-7)
Topical, eye serums, creams and gels

paras: Dipeptide-2 is described as a tiny peptide with only two amino acids, listed under the INCI name Dipeptide-2 with a skin-conditioning function.[1] It is classified as a cell-communicating ingredient and appears mainly in eye-area serums, eye creams and gels, including products aimed at dark circles and wrinkles around the eyes.[1]

The manufacturer's explanation is that the dipeptide boosts lymphatic circulation so that fluid is carried away from the under-eye area, and that combining it with hesperidin methyl chalcone and palmitoyl tetrapeptide-7 gives a broader approach to puffy eyes.[1]

Wikipedia's article on periorbital puffiness lists fluid retention, sleep deprivation, salt intake, allergy and ageing among causes, and describes cold compresses and sleeping with the head raised as common measures; it does not discuss topical peptide products.[2]

No independent studies found. The ingredient's manufacturer reports a small study of 20 volunteers using the Eyeliss complex at 3%, with improvement in 70% after 56 days; it tested the three-active complex rather than dipeptide-2 alone, and the results have not been independently verified.[1]
